title.en: Handle the degenerate cases on purpose

summary: Enumerate the degenerate configurations of a construction and give each an intended, labelled behaviour.
objective: Turn the cases where a construction collapses into part of the explanation instead of a rendering failure.
applies_when: A cutting plane, projection or intersection can reach a special position.
A parameter can reach zero, infinity, a tangency or a coincidence.
The classification of the result is displayed, such as ellipse, parabola or hyperbola.
example_prompts: Show what the section becomes when the plane passes through the apex.
Let me reach the parabola case exactly.
negative_signals: Constructions whose parameters are constrained away from the special cases by design.
Purely decorative geometry where classification is not claimed.
not_for: Constructions whose parameters are constrained away from the special cases by design.
Purely decorative geometry where classification is not claimed.

principles: Degenerate cases are part of the mathematics, not exceptions to it. A plane through the apex of a double cone produces a point, a line or two intersecting lines depending on its angle.
The interesting boundary is often exactly at the transition, so a scene that skips or jitters past it hides the most instructive configuration.
Floating-point comparison decides when a case is reached. Without a stated tolerance, the transition either never occurs or flickers.
A classification label is a claim: if the scene names the curve, the naming must include the degenerate outcomes rather than defaulting to the nearest non-degenerate name.
implementation: Enumerate the degenerate configurations of the construction up front and decide the intended behaviour and label for each.
Snap to or allow exact attainment of the special configuration, with a stated tolerance, so it can actually be inspected.
Render the degenerate result honestly, for example as a point or a pair of lines, rather than an empty view or a collapsed mesh.
Report the classification from the parameters rather than from the produced geometry, which may be empty.
Show the neighbourhood of the transition, for example by allowing slow movement through it, so the viewer sees the case appear.
observable_checks: Sweep the parameter through each special value and check the expected classification on both sides and at the boundary itself; a sweep that leaves and re-enters a regular case changes label more than once, which is correct, so compare against the expected sequence rather than a fixed number of changes.
Land exactly on the degenerate value and confirm the display is intended rather than blank or broken.

Approach from both sides and confirm each side matches its expected case. Asymmetry is often correct: at a tangency the intersection can be empty on one side and non-empty on the other, so do not require a symmetric neighbourhood.
Confirm the stated tolerance is visible, since the transition point depends on it.

creative_affordances: Degenerate cases can be dramatised, for example by holding on the transition, since they are usually the memorable moment of the scene.
A gallery of all cases side by side is a legitimate alternative to a single sweep.
known_limits: Authored guidance citing the classification of degenerate conics; other constructions have their own special cases not enumerated here.
It does not prescribe a numerical tolerance, which depends on the units and scale of the scene.

claims.statement: A degenerate conic results when the intersecting plane passes through the apex of the double cone, and depending on the angle of the plane the result is a point, a line, or two intersecting lines.
claims.scope: Classification of plane sections of a double cone; it does not cover degenerate cases of other surfaces.
